questions.prompt: You build a RAG app on Claude. Where do the embeddings come from?

options.text: From the Messages API, by asking Claude for a vector.
options.explanation: The Claude docs say Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model, so the Messages API is not the place.

options.text: From an embedding provider such as Voyage AI.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic has no embedding model of its own; the Claude docs describe Voyage AI as one provider.

options.text: From Claude's tokenizer, which turns text into numbers.
options.explanation: Token ids are not embeddings. An embedding is a vector where distance measures relatedness.

questions.prompt: OpenAI embeddings are normalized to length 1. What follows from that, per the OpenAI docs?

options.text: You must use Euclidean distance, because cosine similarity fails.
options.explanation: OpenAI recommends cosine similarity. Normalization makes it easier, not impossible.

options.text: Every vector has the same values, so only the text length matters.
options.explanation: Length 1 fixes the size of each vector, not its direction. The direction carries the meaning.

options.text: Cosine similarity and Euclidean distance give identical rankings.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI also notes that cosine similarity can be computed slightly faster with just a dot product.

questions.prompt: The query is: When did we go to the moon? Which text does semantic search rank highest in the OpenAI retrieval guide?

options.text: When I ate the moon cake, it was delicious.
options.explanation: It shares the most words (40% keyword similarity), but its meaning is far away: 28% semantic similarity.

options.text: The first lunar landing occurred in July of 1969.
options.explanation: Right. It shares no words with the query (0% keyword similarity) but scores 65% on semantic similarity.
